verses.text: “Behold, my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delights — I have put my Spirit on him. He will bring justice to the nations.
He will not shout, nor raise his voice, nor cause it to be heard in the street.
He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a dimly burning wick. He will faithfully bring justice.
He will not fail nor be discouraged, until he has set justice in the earth, and the islands will wait for his law.”

Thus says God Yahweh, he who created the heavens and stretched them out, he who spread out the earth and that which comes out of it, he who gives breath to its people and spirit to those who walk in it.
“I, Yahweh, have called you in righteousness, and will hold your hand, and will keep you, and make you a covenant for the people, as a light for the nations;
to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
“I am Yahweh. That is my name. I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to engraved images.
Behold, the former things have happened, and I declare new things. I tell you about them before they come up.”
Sing to Yahweh a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that is therein, the islands and their inhabitants.
Let the wilderness and its cities raise their voices, with the villages that Kedar inhabits. Let the inhabitants of Sela sing. Let them shout from the top of the mountains!
Let them give glory to Yahweh, and declare his praise in the islands.
Yahweh will go out like a mighty man. He will stir up zeal like a man of war. He will raise a war cry. Yes, he will shout aloud. He will triumph over his enemies.
“I have been silent a long time. I have been quiet and restrained myself. Now I will cry out like a travailing woman. I will both gasp and pant.
I will destroy mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs. I will make the rivers islands, and will dry up the pools.

I will bring the blind by a way that they don’t know. I will lead them in paths that they don’t know. I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. I will do these things, and I will not forsake them.
“Those who trust in engraved images, who tell molten images, ‘You are our gods’ will be turned back. They will be utterly disappointed.
“Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see.
Who is blind, but my servant? Or who is as deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is as blind as he who is at peace, and as blind as Yahweh’s servant?
You see many things, but don’t observe. His ears are open, but he doesn’t listen.
It pleased Yahweh, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify the law, and make it honorable.

But this is a robbed and plundered people. All of them are snared in holes, and they are hidden in prisons. They have become captives, and no one delivers; and a plunder, and no one says, ‘Restore them!’
Who is there among you who will give ear to this? Who will listen and hear for the time to come?
Who gave Jacob as plunder, and Israel to the robbers? Didn’t Yahweh, he against whom we have sinned? For they would not walk in his ways, and they disobeyed his law.
Therefore he poured the fierceness of his anger on him, and the strength of battle; and it set him on fire all around, but he didn’t know; and it burned him, but he didn’t take it to heart.”

footnotes.content: The Father speaks over His chosen Servant — the language echoes the voice from heaven at Jesus's baptism. 'My soul delights' is the intimacy of the Father's deepest joy in His Son. Already He declares the Servant's work: justice to the nations, not through force but through the Spirit's anointing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Servant will not bully or make a noise in the streets — no posturing, no desperate self-promotion. Whenever I've seen real authority, it's quiet. The Lord's justice doesn't announce itself with fanfare; it simply comes, steady and unshakeable.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The bruised reed, the smoldering wick — the frailest, most nearly-done things in the kingdom. The Servant will not finish them off with one careless foot. Instead He bends to tenderness, where everyone else sees only kindling for the fire. That's how He binds us to Himself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No defeat, no discouragement — the Servant presses on until justice fills the earth. The islands await His law. There's a steadiness here that doesn't depend on mood or circumstance. He will not tire before the work is done; we are safe in His perseverance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The God who stretches out heavens and spreads earth — the Creator of all breath and spirit — now speaks. His power over creation is the foundation of His promise to the nations. He who made us also knows how to sustain us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Called in righteousness, held by His hand, kept and covenanted as a light to nations — this is safety wrapped in purpose. The Servant is held, not just sent. His hand steadies ours in the darkness we're sent into. A covenant with His people through Him means we never walk that road alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blind eyes opened, prisoners freed from dungeons and darkness — the work of the Servant is always toward the captive and the lost. When Jesus read this in the synagogue, He claimed it as His own work: sight to the blind, freedom to those in chains.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh's name — His very self, His character — cannot be given to another. His glory belongs to no idol, no substitute, no half-god. In a world that endlessly manufactures alternatives to the true God, this is His firm boundary: there is one Name that stands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Former things have come to pass; new things He declares before they arise. The God who speaks beforehand establishes His truth by acting exactly as He promised. In that reliability, we can trust what He says about things not yet seen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A new song from the ends of the earth — sailors, islanders, the far-flung peoples all join in praise. The scope is vast: creation itself is called to worship. This is the longing of every generation: to sing something true that echoes from shore to shore.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wilderness and cities, villages of Kedar, Sela's heights — even the remote and rocky places are summoned to sing and shout from the mountaintops. The Gospel reaches where roads don't go. There's no corner of creation too small or too far for His praise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Glory and praise declared in the islands — the response spreads outward from land to sea, from center to edge. When the heart turns to Yahweh, it spills over. Praise is not meant to stay quiet; it travels.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God goes forth like a mighty warrior, stirring zeal and raising the battle cry, triumphing over enemies. After verses of gentleness with the bruised reed, the tone shifts — this is the other face of justice. Those who oppose His purpose will meet His strength.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Silent a long time, restrained — now He cries out like a woman in labor, gasping and panting. There's urgency here, passion. His silence is not indifference; it's been a held breath. When He speaks, it comes from the deepest place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mountains fall, rivers become islands, pools dry up — His word reshapes the landscape of reality. When God acts, creation itself submits. The impossible is what He does before breakfast.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The blind are led by unknown ways, darkness turns to light, crooked places straighten — and through it all, 'I will not forsake them.' The promise is not that the path will be familiar, but that He will hold their hand the whole way. That's enough.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who trust in carved and molten gods will be turned back and utterly disappointed. We've all felt the emptiness of reaching for what cannot reach back. Idols disappoint because they're just stone; only the living God can hold us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A call to the deaf and blind to listen and look — to wake up. There's urgency in this command: the Spirit is at work, the Servant is coming, and He calls us to perceive it, to stop sleepwalking through grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Servant is described as blind and deaf — a paradox, since He opens blind eyes. His 'blindness' is His humility, His refusal to claim sight that belongs only to the Father. His 'deafness' is His singular listening — to God's voice alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To see many things yet not observe, to have open ears yet not listen — this is the condition of the human heart in rebellion. We walk past grace daily. The tragedy is not blindness of the eye but blindness of the will.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: For righteousness' sake, the law is magnified and made honorable — God exalts what is just and right. His love for justice is not separate from His love for us; justice is how He protects and honors His beloved.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Israel is robbed and plundered, trapped and imprisoned, with no one to deliver or restore. The people lie in captivity — and yet God has not forgotten them. Into this darkness of abandonment, the Servant is coming as Deliverer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Who will listen? Who will hear for the time to come? It's a question posed to the present generation — will we wake to what God is saying now? The warning has weight only if we choose to hear it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jacob and Israel given to robbers — not because God is weak, but because His people wouldn't walk His ways. Sin opens the door to captivity. And yet the question itself carries a note of lament, as if God grieves what disobedience has cost them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo: God poured fierce anger and the strength of battle around them, yet they didn't know it, didn't take it to heart. We miss so much of what God is doing in our lives — the refining fire, the loving corrections — because our hearts are not watching for Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
